onboarding.heading: Welcome to {{app}}
onboarding.introImported: Your products, inventory and order history are imported. Answer two questions and we'll show which products will run out, when, and how many to reorder.
onboarding.introImporting: We're reading your products, inventory and last year's orders so we can tell you which products will run out, when, and how many to reorder. This takes a few minutes; you can answer the questions below meanwhile.
onboarding.leadTimeLabel: How many days does a reorder usually take to arrive?
onboarding.leadTimeHelp: Your typical supplier lead time. You can set it per supplier or per product later.
onboarding.emailLabel: Where should we send stock alerts?
onboarding.emailHelp: One summary email when something needs reordering. Never more than one a day. Leave empty to turn alerts off.

home.preparingBody: We're importing your store data. Your forecast appears here as soon as it's ready.
home.emptyBody: Forecasts need products with tracked inventory. Run a sync after adding products.

slow.summaryWithValue_other: {{value}} is sitting in {{count}} products with more than {{days}} days of stock.

slow.summary_other: {{count}} products have more than {{days}} days of stock.

planLimit.body_other: The Free plan forecasts your {{total}} best sellers. {{count}} more products are not forecast; upgrade to include every product.

tips.label: Tip:
tips.home_actions: Today's products are already ticked. Export purchase order turns them into one file for your supplier.
tips.home_runway: Each bar is how many days of stock are left. The dashed line is when to reorder so new stock arrives in time.
tips.product_explanation: These are the exact numbers behind the forecast. If you know something we don't, adjust the sales rate below.

setup.heading: Get the most out of your forecasts
setup.subheading: A few minutes of setup makes every reorder suggestion more accurate.

import_data.title: Import your store data
import_data.bodyRunning: We're importing your products, inventory and order history. This takes a few minutes.
import_data.body: Products, inventory and a year of orders are imported and refreshed every night.

lead_time.title: Set your default lead time
lead_time.body: How many days a reorder usually takes to arrive. Every reorder date is based on it.

review_forecast.title: See why a product needs reordering
review_forecast.body: Open a product to see how its forecast was built, and adjust the sales rate if you know better (a promotion, a quiet month).

suppliers.title: Add your suppliers and their lead times
suppliers.body: Products from a slower supplier get reordered earlier. You can also export one purchase order per supplier. Coming from Stocky? Import your purchase orders to set this up in one go.
suppliers.fromVendors_one: Create a supplier from your vendor

alerts.title: Turn on stock alerts
alerts.body: One summary email when products need reordering. Never more than one a day.
alerts.lockedBody: Alerts are included in Starter, with a 7-day free trial.

po.shopifyDone: Downloaded. In Shopify, open Products › Purchase orders › Create purchase order and import this file.
po.shopifySkipped_one: {{count}} product has no SKU or barcode and was left out.
po.shopifySkipped_other: {{count}} products have no SKU or barcode and were left out.

why.heading: Why these numbers?
why.locked: See exactly how each forecast is built: which days were used, out-of-stock days left out, seasonality, bundles, lead time and safety stock, in plain language.
why.seasonalityApplied: Seasonality: ×{{factor}} based on the next {{days}} days last year.

seasonalityReasons.not_enough_history: less than a year of sales history
seasonalityReasons.out_of_stock_last_year: the product was often out of stock at this time last year
seasonalityReasons.too_few_sales_last_year: too few sales at this time last year
seasonalityReasons.no_significant_change: no meaningful change at this time last year

locations.heading: By location
locations.pending: Per-location forecasts appear after the next sync (open the app once to approve the new fulfillment permissions if Shopify asks).
locations.hint: Select a location to see why. Sales-rate adjustments apply to the store total only.

adjust.heading: Adjust the sales rate
adjust.intro: Expecting a promotion or a quiet month? Set the sales per day yourself. Our estimate is {{rate}}/day.
adjust.untilHelp: Afterwards we go back to the automatic forecast.

productSettings.heading: Product settings
productSettings.safetyHelp: Extra days of stock kept in case sales jump or a delivery is late.
productSettings.minOrderHelp: The supplier's minimum order in units. Suggestions below it are raised to it.
productSettings.packSizeHelp: Units per case or pack. Suggestions are rounded up to whole packs.
productSettings.minStockHelp: Reorder when stock plus stock on the way falls to this. Leave empty to let the forecast decide.
productSettings.maxStockHelp: Orders fill stock up to this level. Leave empty to let the forecast decide.
productSettings.muteAlerts: Don't send alerts for this product
productSettings.muteAlertsHelp: Leaves it out of summary and real-time emails. Forecasts and the reorder list still include it.

products.freeLimit_one: The Free plan forecasts your best seller.
products.freeLimit_other: The Free plan forecasts your {{count}} best sellers.

settings.defaultsIntro: Used for products without their own lead time or supplier.
settings.leadTimeHelp: How long a reorder usually takes to arrive.
settings.alertsLocked: Get one summary email when products need reordering. Never more than one a day.
settings.alertsEnabled: Email me when products need reordering
settings.frequencyHelp: One summary email, only when something needs attention.
settings.realtimeHelp: An email as soon as stock crosses a threshold. Changes are grouped into one email every 15 minutes, a product is mentioned at most once a week, at most 3 emails a day and never at night.
settings.realtimeOutOfStock: Only when a product sells out
settings.realtimeAll: When a product needs reordering or sells out
settings.realtimeLocked: Hear about a sell-out when it happens, not the next morning. Grouped and capped, so your inbox stays quiet.
settings.setupGuideBack: Setup guide is back on Home
settings.languageHelp: Alert emails are sent in English.

suppliers.name: Name
suppliers.leadTimeHelp: Used for all products from this supplier unless a product has its own lead time.

bundles.locked: Count bundle and kit sales toward each product inside them, so components are reordered in time.
bundles.emptyBody: Selling kits or gift boxes? Tell us what's inside so their sales count toward each product's forecast. Bundles made with Shopify Bundles are picked up automatically.
bundles.modalIntro: When the bundle sells, we count its components as sold too, so their forecasts include bundle sales.

plans.intro: Flat monthly price. No share of your sales, no contract, cancel anytime. Billed by Shopify on your Shopify invoice.
plans.trialNote: {{count}}-day free trial, then billed by Shopify

import.heading: Import suppliers from purchase orders
import.intro: Coming from Stocky? Stocky can't export suppliers, but its purchase orders show who supplies what. Upload them and we'll create your suppliers, link each product to the supplier you last ordered it from, and measure lead times from past deliveries.
import.stepExport: In Stocky, open Purchase orders (or Reports) and export them as CSV. Several files are fine.
import.stepUpload: Drop the files below. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
import.stepCheck: Check the suppliers and lead times we found, then import.
import.otherApps: Purchase order CSVs from other apps or spreadsheets work too, as long as they have a supplier column and a SKU, variant ID or product name column.
import.columnsHelp: We matched these columns automatically. Change any that look wrong.
import.missing: We couldn't find: {{fields}}. Choose the right columns below.

required.product: a product column (SKU, variant ID or product name)

import.notMeasured: No delivery dates: leave empty to use the store default
import.matched_one: {{count}} product will be linked to the supplier it was last ordered from.
import.matched_other: {{count}} products will be linked to the supplier they were last ordered from.
import.unmatched_one: {{count}} row didn't match a product in your store (for example {{samples}}). It is skipped.
import.unmatched_other: {{count}} rows didn't match a product in your store (for example {{samples}}). They are skipped.
import.replace_one: Also replace the supplier of {{count}} product that already has one
import.replace_other: Also replace the supplier of {{count}} products that already have one

supplierEmail.autoHelp: When this supplier's products need ordering, we email them the purchase order (at most once a week, from 8am your time). Replies go to your alert email.

downgrade.heading: Switch to {{plan}}?
downgrade.intro: On this plan, the following stops working for your store:
downgrade.nothingLost: Nothing you use today stops working.
downgrade.kept: Your data and settings are kept. Upgrade again at any time and everything works as before.

lost.bundles_one: Bundle sales no longer count toward component forecasts ({{count}} bundle set up).
lost.bundles_other: Bundle sales no longer count toward component forecasts ({{count}} bundles set up).
lost.alerts: Stock alert emails are not available.
lost.purchase_orders: Purchase order export and emailing orders to suppliers stop.

lost.realtime_alerts: Real-time stock alerts are not available.

vendors.heading: Create suppliers from vendors
vendors.intro: Your Shopify products already have a Vendor. Each vendor you tick becomes a supplier (or uses the supplier with that name) and its products are linked to it. You can add lead times and emails afterwards.
